test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following rivers forms a delta along the Eastern Coastal Plains?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Godavari River is the second-longest river in India after the Ganga, originating from **Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra**.
 
• It flows eastward across the Indian Peninsula and forms a large delta at its mouth before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The delta formed by the Godavari is fertile and supports extensive agriculture, particularly the cultivation of paddy.
 
• The Godavari Delta is one of the largest in India, covering parts of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• Major tributaries of the Godavari include the **Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari, and Manjira** rivers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delta Formation**

 
 
• A delta is a landform created by the deposition of sediment carried by a river as the flow exits its mouth and enters a standing water body like an ocean or sea.
 
• In India, rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi form deltas due to their large sediment loads and slower flow near their mouths.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plains**
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains of India are located between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal.
 
• They are characterized by fertile soils, extensive deltas, and major river systems such as the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River Basin**
 
 
• The Godavari River Basin is one of India's largest river basins, covering parts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The basin supports diverse ecosystems, including forests, agriculture, and wetlands.
 
 
 
• **Major Rivers Not Forming Deltas**
 
 
• Rivers like the Narmada, Tapi, and Mahi do not form deltas but instead create estuaries as they flow into the Arabian Sea.
 
• This is due to their relatively steep gradients and sediment transport patterns.
